sections.content:
60,305 people

were counted on the census as "fork-lift truck drivers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Fork-lift truck drivers operate fork-lift trucks in factories, warehouses, storerooms and other areas to transfer goods and materials.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "fork-lift truck drivers" there were more men than women (97.3% compared with 2.7%).

This means "fork-lift truck drivers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "transport and mobile machine drivers and operatives".

Men made up 97.3% and women made up 2.7% of "fork-lift truck drivers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "fork-lift truck drivers" included:

  • metal working production and maintenance fitters
  • tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out
  • elementary construction occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "fork-lift truck drivers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "fork-lift truck drivers", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "fork-lift truck drivers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "fork-lift truck drivers" included:

  • welfare professionals (other)
  • other educational professionals
  • credit controllers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "fork-lift truck drivers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "fork-lift truck drivers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "fork-lift truck drivers", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.8% compared with 5.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96%) than self-employed (4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
